issues.t: Service High Voltage warning or no start from battery software
issues.sym: A check engine light and a "Service High Voltage" message, sometimes after a long charging session. In some cases the car will not start or go into Ready mode.
issues.why: GM has issued several bulletins blaming software in the battery energy control module, the computer that manages the big battery. Long, uninterrupted charging sessions and charging interruptions can trigger the fault codes.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the codes and reprogram the battery control module, and accept over-the-air updates. GM also suggests unplugging the car for at least 20 minutes a day rather than leaving it charging for days.

issues.t: 12-volt battery drains with Service High Voltage message
issues.sym: A dead or weak 12-volt battery, a check engine light, or a "Service High Voltage" message. The car may not power on.
issues.why: A calibration problem in the battery control module can keep systems awake and run down the small 12-volt battery that starts up the car.
issues.next: Have the 12-volt battery charged and tested, and ask the dealer about GM bulletin PIP6021, which covers a software update and reset.

issues.t: Unable to charge or DC fast charging unavailable
issues.sym: An "Unable to Charge" message, a "Service High Voltage" warning, or DC fast chargers that will not start a session even though home charging still works.
issues.why: Software errors, snow, ice or moisture in the charge port, plugging in while the car is not in Park, or a fault in the fast-charge wiring can set code P2980 and lock out fast charging.
issues.next: Make sure the car is in Park and the charge port is clean and dry before plugging in. If the warning stays, a dealer can diagnose code P2980 and update the software.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking slams on with nothing ahead
issues.sym: The car brakes hard on the highway or at moderate speed with no vehicle or obstacle in front, sometimes with a forward collision alert. Drivers behind can be put at risk.
issues.why: Owners have filed many NHTSA complaints about the forward automatic braking system reacting to things that are not there. Some events follow a "camera blocked" message.
issues.next: Keep the windshield camera area and front sensors clean, install software updates, and report every event to the dealer and to NHTSA. Leave extra room behind you if it has happened before.

issues.t: Hard automatic braking while backing up
issues.sym: The car brakes suddenly and hard while reversing, especially in rain, with nothing behind it.
issues.why: The rear automatic braking feature can be triggered by rain or reflections behind the car.
issues.next: Report it to a dealer for a sensor check and software update. You can turn off rear automatic braking in settings, but then check carefully before reversing.

issues.t: Sudden loss of drive power while driving
issues.sym: The car stops accelerating or loses all drive power and regenerative braking while moving, sometimes at highway speed. Restarting the car may bring it back.
issues.why: Owners report power losses from several causes, including high-voltage battery faults that needed battery replacement. Some specific causes are covered by recalls listed separately.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Steer to the shoulder and turn on your hazards. Check for open recalls, and have a dealer pull the stored codes even if the car seems fine after a restart.

issues.t: Instrument display dims too much at dusk
issues.sym: The driver display and center screen dim so far at sunset, under bridges or in shade that they are hard to read, and are slow to brighten again.
issues.why: The automatic brightness control reacts too strongly to outside light, and owners say there is no way to turn it off or set it manually.
issues.next: Report it to a dealer and keep the software up to date. Mention it if your car also has the blank-display recall, which is a separate problem.

issues.t: Infotainment and connectivity keep dropping out
issues.sym: Bluetooth, phone charging, Wi-Fi or the radio disconnect over and over, the screen freezes or reboots, or the gauges show the wrong speed or gear for a moment.
issues.why: These are software problems in the infotainment and display system. Some owners report several repair visits before they were fixed.
issues.next: Install all over-the-air updates. If it keeps happening, keep a log of each event and ask the dealer to escalate it to GM.

issues.t: OnStar and connectivity lost from failed telematics module
issues.sym: OnStar, GPS and the app connection stop working, and the car cannot call for help after a crash.
issues.why: The telematics module, which handles the car's cellular connection, can fail. Owners report replacement parts on backorder.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the module has failed and order the part. Carry your phone so you can call for help yourself until it is fixed.

issues.t: A/C compressor makes a loud chopping noise
issues.sym: A loud chopping or knocking noise from the front of the car when the A/C or heat pump runs.
issues.why: The electric A/C compressor, which also helps heat and cool the battery, can become noisy.
issues.next: Have the dealer check it under warranty, since the compressor also helps manage battery temperature.

issues.t: Low-beam headlight flickers on and off
issues.sym: One low-beam headlight flickers or switches on and off, even while parked.
issues.why: A dealer was able to reproduce the flicker but a software update, wiring checks and a new headlamp did not cure it on at least one car.
issues.next: Report it to the dealer with a video of the flicker, and keep records in case the repair takes more than one visit.

issues.t: Adaptive cruise surges ahead when resuming after a stop
issues.sym: After stopping behind traffic with cruise on, a light tap on the accelerator makes the car leap forward hard.
issues.why: Adaptive cruise control resumes its set speed after a stop, even when the driver has turned toward another lane.
issues.next: Be ready to brake when resuming cruise after a stop, and report the behavior to the dealer and NHTSA.

issues.t: Brake control software can reduce braking (recall)
issues.sym: Brakes that feel weaker or respond less than expected in some conditions.
issues.why: A software defect in the brake control module can reduce braking response; the recall covers about 67,000 GM EVs (NHTSA 26V-717).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. The fix is a software update, over the air or at a dealer.

issues.t: ABS can activate on its own and lengthen stops (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal pulses as if on ice while braking on dry pavement, and the car takes longer to stop.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake system on all-wheel-drive models can activate unexpectedly and release brake pressure (NHTSA 24V589000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. The fix is a free brake control module software update.

issues.t: Driver display can go blank while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The driver display goes dark, so you lose the speedometer, warning lights and rear camera view.
issues.why: The video display control module software can blank the screen (NHTSA 25V356000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. The dealer or an over-the-air update installs new display software for free.

issues.t: Instrument panel can go blank from display software (recall)
issues.sym: The instrument panel goes dark on early 2023 cars.
issues.why: A software error in the video display control module on early 2023 Lyriqs can blank the instrument panel (NHTSA 22V710000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. GM updates the software for free.

issues.t: Rear seat belt anchor bracket may be badly welded (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom; the left-rear and center-rear belts may not hold in a crash.
issues.why: The bracket for two rear seat belts may not be properly welded to the seat frame (NHTSA 23V785000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. Do not use those two seats until a dealer replaces the rear seat cushion frame for free.

issues.t: High-voltage battery welds can cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: Battery or propulsion warnings and a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: Connections inside the battery pack may be out of position or badly welded (NHTSA 23V367000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. The dealer inspects the pack and replaces it if needed, free.

issues.t: Pedestrian warning sound may not play (recall)
issues.sym: No outside humming sound at low speed, so people nearby may not hear the car.
issues.why: The body control module was loaded with wrongly calibrated software (NHTSA 23V682000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. The dealer reprograms the module for free.

issues.t: Rear motor wiring can short and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: Wires inside the rear drive motor may not be insulated well enough and can touch (NHTSA 24V320000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. The dealer replaces the rear drive unit for free.

issues.t: Front stabilizer bar bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front suspension. If cables or coolant lines are damaged, the car can shut down.
issues.why: Front stabilizer bar bracket bolts may be under-tightened and can loosen, damaging high-voltage cables or battery coolant lines (NHTSA 25V232000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. The dealer checks and tightens the bolts for free.

issues.t: Battery pack mounting bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs in normal driving.
issues.why: Bolts holding the high-voltage battery to the car may be missing or loose, which raises the risk of battery damage and fire in a crash (NHTSA 25V483000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. The dealer inspects and tightens or replaces the bolts, free.

issues.t: Rearview camera screen turns gray (recall)
issues.sym: The screen turns gray with no camera image when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: The display may fail to show the rear camera image (NHTSA 26V082000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. The fix is a free software update, over the air or at a dealer.

issues.t: Owner's manual has wrong head restraint information (recall)
issues.sym: No mechanical symptom; you may set the rear outer head restraints wrong if you follow the manual.
issues.why: The owner's manual describes the rear outboard head restraints incorrectly (NHTSA 25V193000).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. GM mails a corrected manual insert.

issues.t: Electronic owner's manual may not download (recall)
issues.sym: The owner's manual is missing from the center screen.
issues.why: The radio may not download the electronic owner's manual (NHTSA 26V-114).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at nhtsa.gov, in the myCadillac app or with a dealer. The dealer resets the radio for free.
